sentenceFrames.text: I believe colleges should encourage students to ____.
One practical benefit of ____ is that ____.
A better approach is to make ____ available while allowing students to ____.

templates.sampleEssay:
Volunteer work deserves a regular place in college life. A university should encourage students to take part, while leaving them free to choose an activity that fits their interests and schedule.

One benefit is that students practise skills that rarely appear on written exams. A student who helps at a food bank has to listen carefully, explain tasks clearly, and work with people of different ages. These experiences can make group projects on campus easier as well. Another benefit is that local organisations gain a steady supply of help. If a campus club agrees to cover two shifts each month, a community centre can plan its services around a dependable team.

The college can support these partnerships by advertising opportunities in a single place and offering short training sessions before students begin. It should also invite volunteers to reflect on what they learned. This approach gives students a reason to return and gives organisations the continuity they need.

sentenceFrames.text: Although ____ is convenient, it can lead to ____.
To address ____, canteens could ____.
The success of these measures could be judged by ____.

templates.sampleEssay:
At lunchtime, many college canteens serve rice in standard portions. This makes the queue move quickly, but it also leaves food on the plates of students who are less hungry. Some waste occurs even earlier when kitchens prepare more meals than they can sell.

The first change could be to let customers choose a small or regular portion at the counter. The smaller size could cost slightly less, so students would have a reason to consider how much they need. The second change would involve counting meals sold each day and comparing the figures with the academic calendar. A kitchen could then reduce production on days when many classes are cancelled and prepare more on busy days.

Both changes can be tested in one canteen for a month. Staff should weigh leftovers and ask customers whether they can still get the meals they want. If waste falls without long queues or frequent shortages, the university can expand the programme.

sentenceFrames.text: The survey compares ____ in ____ and ____.
The share of ____ rose from ____ to ____.
One possible explanation for this change is ____.

templates.sampleEssay:
A campus survey asked students how they usually travelled to class in 2022 and again in 2025. The most striking result was the increase in cycling. The percentage of students who usually rode a bike doubled from 12 percent to 24 percent.

The other three methods became somewhat less popular. Bus travel fell from 38 percent to 33 percent, although it was still the most common choice in 2025. Walking dropped by three percentage points to 31 percent, while driving fell from 16 percent to 12 percent. The combined share of walking and cycling nevertheless increased, from 46 percent to 55 percent.

One possible explanation is that a safer cycle route made short journeys easier. The figures alone cannot tell us whether students actually used such a route or whether other factors, such as changes in housing, mattered more. A later survey could ask students why they chose each method and where they started their journeys.

sentenceFrames.text: I am writing to ask whether ____.
A practical arrangement would be to ____.
Thank you for considering ____. I would be happy to ____.

templates.sampleEssay:
Dear Library Manager,

I am writing on behalf of students who use the main reading room to ask whether it could stay open until ten in the evening during the two weeks before final exams.

Several evening classes finish shortly before the library closes. Students in those classes have little time to review notes or use the reference books that cannot be borrowed. The study rooms in our residence halls are often full at this time of year, so they offer limited help.

A practical arrangement would be to keep only the ground floor open after eight. Students could enter with their campus cards, and the borrowing desk could keep its normal hours. Our student association can share the temporary schedule and remind users to leave quietly. We can also collect feedback about demand during the trial.

Thank you for considering this request. I would be happy to provide the results of our short survey or discuss the plan with your team.

Yours sincerely,
Chen Lin

sentenceFrames.text: The line graph compares ____ over the period from ____ to ____.
Overall, both figures ____, with ____ remaining higher throughout.
After falling to ____, the figure recovered to ____ by ____.

templates.sampleEssay:
The line graph compares annual attendance at the City Museum and the Maritime Museum over the five years from 2019 to 2023. Visitor figures are given in thousands.

Overall, both museums recorded a decline in the second year, followed by three consecutive years of growth. The City Museum attracted more visitors every year. Its lead was smallest in 2020 and 2021 and reached its widest point at the end of the period.

In 2019, the City Museum welcomed 120,000 people, compared with 90,000 at the Maritime Museum. Attendance then fell by 40,000 at the City Museum and by 30,000 at the Maritime Museum. The two figures increased by the same amount in 2021, rising by 15,000 each to reach 95,000 and 75,000 respectively. At that stage, neither venue had returned to its opening figure.

The recovery accelerated in 2022. The City Museum added another 35,000 visitors and reached 130,000, while a rise of 25,000 brought the Maritime Museum to 100,000. Both totals were now above their 2019 levels. In the final year, attendance at the City Museum rose by a further 30,000 to a peak of 160,000. The Maritime Museum gained 10,000 visitors in the same year, bringing its figure to 110,000 and leaving a gap of 50,000.

templates.sampleEssay:
The bar chart compares the proportions of commuters who walk, cycle, take a bus or drive in three districts, namely North, Central and South.

Overall, the most common mode varies across the three districts. Bus travel leads in North, driving leads in South, and walking and bus travel are equally common in Central. The largest geographical differences are in driving and walking, whereas cycling varies by only ten percentage points.

In North, four out of every ten commuters take the bus. This is ten percentage points more than the share who drive, which stands at 30 percent. Walking accounts for a further 20 percent, and cycling is the least common option, at 10 percent. In Central, walking and bus travel each represent 35 percent of journeys. Cycling and driving also have equal shares there, with each accounting for 15 percent. This is the lowest recorded share for car travel among the three districts.

South has the highest share of drivers at 45 percent, three times the Central figure. The bus is the second most popular mode in South, although its share of 25 percent is the lowest bus figure shown. One fifth of commuters cycle in this district, twice the North proportion. Walking ranks last in South at 10 percent.

sentenceFrames.text: The pie charts show how ____ was divided among ____ in ____ and ____.
Overall, ____ remained the largest item, while ____ gained the most ground.
The proportion spent on ____ increased by ____ percentage points.

templates.sampleEssay:
The two pie charts show how a library allocated its budget across four categories in 2020 and 2025. The categories are staff, collections, digital services and events.

Overall, staffing took the largest share of the budget in both years. The most substantial change was the growth of the digital services allocation, which rose above collections to become the second largest item by 2025. Events accounted for the smallest share in both charts, and that share stayed the same.

In 2020, staff costs represented 40 percent of the budget. Collections followed at 35 percent, only five percentage points behind. These two categories together absorbed three quarters of the available budget. Digital services took 15 percent, and events made up the remaining 10 percent. At this point, the collections share was more than double the digital services figure.

By 2025, the staff allocation had slipped by two percentage points to 38 percent. The collections share saw a much steeper decrease, falling by ten points to 25 percent. Together, staff and collections then represented 63 percent of the budget. Over the same period, digital services rose from 15 to 27 percent, placing the category two points above collections and eleven points below staffing. The allocation for events remained at 10 percent.

sentenceFrames.text: The table provides figures for ____ in ____ in two different years.
Most countries saw ____, with ____ the sole exception.
The largest increase was recorded in ____, where the figure rose by ____ percentage points.

templates.sampleEssay:
The table compares the percentage of electricity supplied by renewable sources in four countries in 2015 and 2025. The countries shown are Arden, Bellin, Cuvera and Dalen.

Overall, the share of renewable electricity rose in three of the countries, with Dalen recording a slight decrease. Bellin had the highest figure in both years. Cuvera increased its renewable share by the widest margin and moved ahead of Dalen, despite having the lowest figure initially.

In 2015, renewables accounted for 48 percent of electricity in Bellin. This was considerably higher than in Dalen, which ranked second at 30 percent. Arden followed with a share of 22 percent, and Cuvera came last at 15 percent. The difference between the highest and lowest figures was therefore 33 percentage points at the beginning of the period.

By 2025, Bellin had reached 55 percent, a rise of seven percentage points. Arden recorded a stronger increase of 15 points and ranked second at 37 percent. Cuvera moved up to third place after a rise of 18 points, to 33 percent. Dalen, meanwhile, saw its share edge down from 30 to 29 percent. The gap between Bellin and the lowest ranked country narrowed to 26 points, and Bellin was still the only country in which renewables provided more than half of electricity.

sentenceFrames.text: The diagram illustrates how ____ is collected and used for ____.
The system starts with ____ and ends with ____, while surplus water is diverted to ____.
Once ____ has passed through ____, it flows into ____.

templates.sampleEssay:
The diagram shows how rainwater is collected from the roof of a shed and used to water plants in a community garden. The system consists of a roof, a series of gutters, a screen, a storage tank, a gravel bed and a hose.

Overall, water moves from the roof to the storage tank through a filter, and most of it is intended for irrigation. When the tank reaches its capacity, the surplus takes a separate route into a gravel bed. The storage tank is consequently the point at which the two routes separate.

During rainfall, water lands on the shed roof and runs down into gutters along the lower edges. The gutters direct the flow towards a screen. As the rainwater passes through the screen, leaves are trapped and the filtered water continues to the tank. Water can then remain in the tank until it is needed. If more water arrives after the tank is full, it leaves through the overflow outlet and drains into the nearby gravel bed.

For irrigation, a hose is connected to the outlet used to draw water from the tank. Gardeners open this outlet and guide the water through the hose to the plants. Water entering the gravel bed and water reaching the plants thus come from the same roof but leave the tank through different outlets.

sentenceFrames.text: I support ____ in workplaces where ____.
Reducing ____ can improve ____ when ____.
A shorter week could create difficulties for ____ unless ____.
On balance, employers should ____ where ____.

templates.sampleEssay:
A four-day working week is often presented as a way to improve life outside the office. I support its introduction where employers can maintain service and reduce total working hours. An arrangement that simply moves the same hours into longer days offers less convincing benefits.

The clearest advantage is that employees gain a predictable block of time for rest and personal commitments. Workers can schedule medical appointments or care for relatives without repeatedly requesting time off. A shorter week can also prompt managers to examine how time is spent. For instance, an office that replaces several routine meetings with written updates may preserve its output despite working fewer hours. Employees also have a direct reason to help identify inefficient practices if the reform gives them more time of their own.

Some organisations face genuine constraints. A clinic must see patients every weekday, and a short week for each employee cannot mean shorter opening hours. Staggered schedules might preserve coverage, but a clinic that already struggles to recruit staff could find the change expensive. In hospitals, for example, managers would need to check that weekend and evening shifts are shared fairly and that the trial does not increase pressure on temporary staff. Employers should therefore run a time-limited trial and measure outcomes such as waiting times, overtime and staff retention before making a permanent commitment.

In summary, the four-day week is worth trying wherever productivity and coverage can be measured. The goal should be to protect workers' time while continuing to meet the needs of customers and the public.

sentenceFrames.text: While some argue for ____, others favour ____. In my view, ____.
A case for teaching ____ is that students can ____.
Studying ____ helps learners understand wider patterns such as ____.
A curriculum that connects ____ with ____ can ____.

templates.sampleEssay:
School timetables leave limited room for history, which raises the question of whether students should spend more time on their own region or on global events. Both approaches offer educational value. I favour a curriculum that introduces historical methods through nearby examples and then applies those methods to wider developments.

Supporters of local history argue that familiar places make the past easier to investigate. A class studying the growth of its town could compare old street maps with current ones and interview residents who remember when a railway station closed. This gives students experience of working with evidence they can find themselves. Lessons can also help them understand why buildings or places matter to different groups in the community.

World history offers a perspective that a single town or country cannot provide. A study of trade, for example, can show that changes in local factories sometimes depend on technology, labour and consumer demand across several continents. Looking at different regions also helps students see that one explanation may fit a particular period without applying everywhere.

Schools can connect these aims within a single unit. A project about a local market might begin with records of the goods once sold there and then trace how suppliers and trading routes changed. Students could then compare their findings with records from another town and explain why similar trading changes produced different results in the two places. This structure gives students a familiar starting point while developing the broader perspective they need to explain change.

sentenceFrames.text: The spread of ____ offers benefits for ____, although it also creates ____.
One advantage is that ____ can make it easier for ____ to ____.
A major drawback arises when ____, particularly in ____.
The overall value of ____ depends on ____.

templates.sampleEssay:
Shared bicycles allow residents and visitors to hire a bike for a short journey and return it near their destination. These schemes can make urban transport more flexible. They also create costs and practical problems that a city needs to consider in advance.

One advantage is that a short bicycle trip can connect passengers with a rail station that is slightly too far away to reach on foot. This makes public transport more useful for homes and workplaces beyond the immediate station area. Shared bicycles also give occasional riders access to a bike without the cost of buying and storing one. In districts with safe cycle lanes, some short car trips may consequently become unnecessary.

The benefits are harder to deliver when bicycles are unevenly distributed. Commuters tend to travel in the same direction at certain times, so one station can fill up while another runs out of bikes. Moving bikes between stations requires staff and vehicles. Parking can also become a problem when riders leave bikes on narrow pavements, where they can block people using wheelchairs or pushing prams. Usage data can reveal where extra bikes are needed, but collecting and interpreting those data also takes staff time and adds to the operating costs. The city may need to pay for designated parking areas and enforce parking rules.

On balance, bike sharing can improve access to transport when it is treated as part of the wider network. Its value depends on safe routes, reliable bike availability and parking that keeps pavements clear.

sentenceFrames.text: Welcome to ____. Let me show you what has changed since ____.
On the ____ side, ____ has been replaced by ____.
I invite you to try ____ and share your suggestions by ____.

templates.sampleEssay:
Good afternoon, everyone. Thank you for joining us to open the redesigned campus courtyard. The two maps on this board show how we have made room for both movement and study.

The west gate is still in the same place, but the narrow path from it has been widened all the way to the library. This should make it easier for students going in opposite directions to pass one another. On the eastern side, sheltered study tables now stand where there was an unused lawn. They will be available for small group meetings even on rainy days. The bicycle racks that used to occupy the southern side have been moved to the entrances of the residence halls, where many riders begin their journeys.

Please take a few minutes to walk through the courtyard today. If you find a spot that still feels crowded, mark it on the map beside the gate. The student council will use those comments when it reviews the new layout next month.

sentenceFrames.text: The line chart tracks ____, while the table compares ____.
Overall, ____ increased, whereas the rate for ____ fell.
The figure rose from ____ to ____, an increase of ____.
The gap between ____ and ____ widened to ____ percentage points.

templates.sampleEssay:
The line chart records the number of registrations for a workshop series from April to June. The accompanying table shows what percentage of registrants attended, with separate figures for online and in-person bookings.

Overall, registrations increased steadily over the period. Attendance rates followed different paths according to how people registered. The rate among online registrants declined, while the rate among those who booked in person rose slightly. In-person bookings had the higher attendance rate in all three months.

The series attracted 120 registrations in April. This figure increased by 40 in May, reaching 160, and rose by another 40 to 200 in June. The final total was therefore about two thirds higher than the initial figure, with equal numerical increases in the two intervals.

In April, 75 per cent of online registrants attended, compared with 80 per cent of those who signed up in person. In May, the online figure fell to 70 per cent, while its in-person counterpart edged up to 82 per cent. The divergence was greatest in June, when online attendance dropped a further ten percentage points to 60 per cent and the in-person rate reached 85 per cent. By the end of the period, the gap had grown from five percentage points to twenty-five.

sentenceFrames.text: The rise in ____ can be traced to ____, and it could be addressed by ____.
One reason items are left behind is that ____.
Shops could address this by ____ before ____.
Together, these measures would make it easier for customers to ____.

templates.sampleEssay:
Repair shops sometimes finish work on goods that their owners never collect. Uncertainty about the final bill and difficulty arranging collection can both contribute to this problem. Shops can address these causes by confirming costs in advance and making collection more flexible.

Customers often bring in a broken item before knowing whether it is worth repairing. When the eventual bill approaches the price of a replacement, some may avoid returning to the shop. Others intend to collect their property but cannot do so during opening hours. A commuter who dropped off a lamp on a day off, for instance, may struggle to return before the shop closes. A single notice sent weeks later can also be easy to overlook.

Shops could agree a maximum price with each customer and seek fresh approval before exceeding it. This gives customers a chance to decline expensive work before labour and materials have been used. Once a repair is complete, a reminder should give the balance due and offer a choice of collection times. Small businesses that cannot open late every day could set aside one evening a week for collections. Where appropriate, customers could also authorise a friend to pick up the item.

The aim is to make the commitment clear when the item is dropped off and to make it easy to keep once the work is done. Price approval reduces the chance of an unexpected bill, while reminders and flexible collection address the practical reasons why repaired goods are left behind. Together, these measures can reduce the amount of stock that shops have to store.
